chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The dowry of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for his wives was twelve Uqiyyah and one Nash, and the Uqiyyah is forty Dirhams, and the Nash is half the Uqiyyah, and it is twenty Dirhams.'

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةً: A unit of weight/currency, here defined as 40 Dirhams
key_terms.مَهَرَ: Dowry (mahr) given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.نَشّاً: A unit of weight/currency, half of an Uqiyyah

ai.seo_question: What was the specific dowry amount given by Prophet Muhammad to his wives according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) regarding the dowry (mahr) given to his wives, specifying a total of 12 Uqiyyah and a Nash. By defining these monetary units in terms of Dirhams, it provides a concrete jurisprudential benchmark for calculating mahr in Shia fiqh. This precedent underscores the Prophet's role in setting practical standards for marital financial obligations within the early Muslim community.
